newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUG 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUG 8.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - According to estimates banks spent 508 million crowns on advertising and sponsoring in 1996. Despite calls for austerity from the government, banks are not expected to change their spending policies this year since most if not all advertising and sponsoring contracts have been signed.

- Delays continue in the division of federal property. CSOB for example yesterday filed legal proceedings against the Slovak Republic which has failed to pay back the bank 14 billion crowns owed since 1993.

- Despite experiencing several fluctuations yesterday, the crown generally maintained a steady course closing at 18.44 to the mark. This represents a two heller increase from when trading began at the begining of the day.

- Vitkovice a.s. and German industrial giant Krupp signed a contract yesterday with Severoceske doly Chomutov to supply heavy machinery. The mining equipment is valued at 1.8-1.9 billion crowns and will be paid for internally by Severoceske doly Chomutov.
- Ceska rafinerska said that a weaker crown and rising world oil prices are responsible for gasoline price increases at gas pumps. Global fuel prices have increased by 40 bollars per tonne.

- Coporate profits are expected to show a year-on-year decline in 1997 thanks to higher interest rates on loans. According to the Industry and Trade Ministry, one third of industrial companies suffered losses in 1996. First quarter results for 1997 indicate that the trend is continuing.

- The PGRLF, a fund for set up to provide support and guarantees to the agricultural and forestry sector will increase subsidies to farmers affected by flooding by three percent. Up until the announcement, standard subsidies were set at 10 percent, while in more severely affectede regions such as Bruntal they were as high as 15 percent.
- Ceska sporitelna is not concerned about outstanding loans in Slovakia. According to bank officials, Slovakia has a good international credit rating.

- According to Viktoria Hradska, CEO of the RDP Group, there is little hope the two existing arms makers associations will merge. Hradska said that only one arms makers association should represent the country abroad.
- The unemployment rate increased month-on-month, rising from 4 percent to 4.3 percent at the end of July. This represents a year-on-year increase of 1.3 percent.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The already intense competition on the Czech mobile telephone market between EuroTel and RadioMobil is expected to increase after the year 2000 when the Cesky telecomunikacni urad opens the market to a third competitor.
LIDOVE NOVINY - One fifth of companies in Southern Moravia affected by flooding are facing the possibility of bankruptcy. Flood damage in the region is estimated at 1.5 billion crowns.

PRAVO - The Czech Statistical Office reported that debt of Czech companies at the end of the first quarter in 1997 exceeded 130 billion crowns. Insolvency in the industrial sector alone now exceeds 27 billion crowns.
